Mentoring for young people

Building brighter futures, with someone by your side.

Future Built Mentoring helps young people feel more confident in themselves, supporting their learning and emotional wellbeing so they can build positive relationships and brighter futures.

What we do

Support tailored to each young person’s needs, life experiences and current circumstance.

Every young person’s story is different. We take time to understand their experiences, strengths and challenges, shaping our support around what matters to them. Whatever their circumstances, we’re here to listen and help them take their next steps with confidence.

1:1 Mentoring

Regular sessions with consistent mentors who take time to listen, build trust and offer encouragement to help each young person grow in confidence and work towards their goals.

  • Setting personal goals and celebrating progress, one step at a time.
  • Building confidence through a trusting, supportive relationship.
  • Working through challenges and developing positive coping skills.
Enquire about 1:1 mentoring →

School & Provision Support

Working in partnership with schools and alternative provision settings to offer personalised mentoring that helps young people overcome barriers to learning, improve attendance and feel more engaged in their education.

  • Working closely with school staff to review progress and support each pupil’s needs.
  • Personalised support to build confidence and engagement in learning.
  • Helping young people overcome challenges affecting attendance.
Get in touch →
Our mentoring process

Taking the next steps, together.

A clear, supportive process that helps young people, parents and schools feel informed and confident about what happens next.

  1. Referral

    Referrals welcomed from parents, carers, schools and professionals seeking support for a young person.

  2. Meeting us

    Welcoming first meet to understand interests, needs and hopes.

  3. Planning

    A personalised plan will be developed, including the young person’s voice and any necessary information.

  4. Sessions begin

    Regular mentoring sessions will begin with consistent mentors, providing practical guidance tailored to the young person’s needs and goals.

  5. Progression

    Regular progress reviews to be carried out, assessing any further need, celebrating achievements and adapting sessions where needed.

FAQs

A little more information to help you feel at home.

What ages do you work with?

Future Built Mentoring supports children and young people aged 4–18, with mentoring tailored to their age, individual needs and stage of development.

Where do sessions take place?

Sessions can take place at our welcoming mentoring unit, as well as in schools and suitable community settings, depending on each young person’s needs and agreed support plan.

How do you keep young people safe?

Young people’s safety and wellbeing come first. Sessions are planned around individual needs, with clear safeguarding procedures and dedicated safeguarding leads. The team works closely with families and schools, listens to concerns and acts promptly when support is needed.

How long does mentoring last?

The length of mentoring depends on each young person’s needs and goals. Progress is reviewed together with families and schools to agree the right support and next steps.

Can a young person refer themselves?

Referrals are made through a parent, carer, school or supporting professional. Young people interested in mentoring can ask a trusted adult to get in touch on their behalf.

Do you work with schools and councils?

Yes, we work with schools and local councils to provide mentoring tailored to each young person’s needs, supporting their education, confidence and emotional wellbeing.
